correctness.rationale: For a hyperedge of size r with m ones, direct conditional expectation gives E DeltaK=0 and E(DeltaK)^2=m(r-m); summing edges yields L H=-sum_ij w_ij 1_{different}. The n singleton and choose(n,2) doubleton cuts force w_ij=lambda if LH=-lambda H for all binary states. The bounded martingale, absorbing-state inequalities and Dynkin argument give all consequences. Exact rational reconstruction and full 128-state verification for each seven-node model check every pair, generator action, off-block lump transition, and rational mean-time equation; an additional nonconstant-weight four-node test checks the general identity. The proof quantifies all n, all finite static hypergraphs, positive edge rates and all deterministic binary starts. Numerical sampling is not used for the theorem.

value.rationale: A natural two-design/pair-codegree characterization tells exactly when the total disagreement closes as one scalar exponential for every initial opinion arrangement. The Fano-plane example then gives a concrete, mathematically natural limitation of pairwise incidence summaries: identical all-time population first and second moments coexist with strictly unequal exact consensus times. This is a structural distinction in higher-order collective copying and not an arbitrary finite slice or merely a known design enumeration. The 13/210 gap is a calculable witness of the failure of moment closure to determine absorption behavior.
